title: When Friendship Becomes Long-Distance
title_ja: 離れてから変わる友情

source_links.title: UNICEF: 11 Tips for Communicating with Your Teen

fact_notes: 背景となる考え方は添付の資料で確認。本文と練習問題は新規制作。例示した人物・学校・活動は架空の説明用設定。

sentences.en: Two friends have studied together since their first year of high school, sharing school activities and ordinary conversations after class.
sentences.ja: 二人の友人は高校一年から共に学び、学校行事や放課後の何気ない会話を共有してきました。

sentences.en: When one family moves to another city, they promise to stay in touch through messages and occasional video calls.
sentences.ja: 一方の家族が別の市へ引っ越すと、二人はメッセージや時折のビデオ通話で連絡を保つと約束します。

sentences.en: However, their daily schedules gradually become different, and one friend starts answering messages much later than before.
sentences.ja: しかし毎日の予定は徐々に異なり、一方の返信が以前よりずっと遅くなります。

sentences.en: The other student begins to worry that the friendship is becoming less important.
sentences.ja: もう一人の生徒は友情の重要性が薄れているのではと心配し始めます。

sentences.en: A delayed response may feel personal even when it has a practical explanation that the reader cannot see.
sentences.ja: 返信の遅れは読み手には見えない実際の理由があっても個人的に感じられることがあります。

sentences.en: Understanding a friendship from a distance requires avoiding conclusions based on a single missing message.
sentences.ja: 離れた友情を理解するには一通の未返信だけで結論を出さないことが必要です。

sentences.en: Instead of accusing the friend of losing interest, the student asks how life at the new school is going.
sentences.ja: 相手が関心を失ったと責める代わりに、生徒は新しい学校での生活を尋ねます。

sentences.en: For example, the friend explains that new club activities and a longer journey home leave little free time on weekdays.
sentences.ja: 例えば友人は新しい部活動と長い帰宅時間で平日の自由時間が少ないと説明します。

sentences.en: The student learns that the late replies are not necessarily signs of a weaker relationship.
sentences.ja: 生徒は返信の遅れが必ずしも関係の弱まりの印ではないと学びます。

sentences.en: UNICEF guidance on communication emphasizes listening carefully and trying to understand another person's feelings and perspective.
sentences.ja: UNICEFのコミュニケーションに関する案内は丁寧に聞き相手の感情や視点を理解することを重視します。

sentences.en: The friends agree to share interesting experiences without expecting an immediate response to every message.
sentences.ja: 二人はすべてのメッセージに即時返信を求めず、おもしろい経験を共有することにします。

sentences.en: Their new arrangement respects the reality that people can care about one another while living different daily lives.
sentences.ja: 新しい取り決めは異なる日常を送りながら互いを大切にできるという現実を尊重します。

sentences.en: The friends also realize that friendship involves more than maintaining a constant stream of online communication.
sentences.ja: 二人は友情はオンラインの連絡を絶やさないこと以上のものだと気づきます。

sentences.en: In addition, they need room to develop new relationships and participate fully in activities at their separate schools.
sentences.ja: さらにそれぞれの学校で新しい関係を築き活動に十分参加する余地も必要です。

sentences.en: A friendship that requires someone to be constantly available may create pressure instead of emotional support.
sentences.ja: 常に連絡可能であることを求める友情は感情的な支援でなく負担を生むかもしれません。

sentences.en: The students decide that occasionally arranging a longer conversation may be better than measuring closeness by daily message counts.
sentences.ja: 毎日のメッセージ数で親密さを測るより、時々長い会話を計画する方がよいかもしれないと考えます。

sentences.en: They also discuss what to do if one person needs urgent help and when a trusted adult should be contacted.
sentences.ja: 緊急の助けが必要な場合や信頼できる大人に連絡すべきときについても話し合います。

sentences.en: Clear expectations can reduce misunderstandings while leaving both people freedom to grow.
sentences.ja: 明確な期待は誤解を減らしつつ双方の成長する自由を残します。

sentences.en: Months later, the friends meet during a school holiday and discover that their interests have changed in different ways.
sentences.ja: 数か月後、休暇に再会した二人は関心がそれぞれ違う形で変わっていると気づきます。

sentences.en: They still enjoy talking, but they no longer share every experience or remember every small event in the other's life.
sentences.ja: 会話は楽しくても互いのすべての経験や小さな出来事を共有してはいません。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, they recognize that change does not automatically mean the end of a meaningful relationship.
sentences.ja: それでも変化が意味ある関係の終わりを自動的に意味するわけではないと理解します。

sentences.en: They can ask questions, learn about new interests, and accept that shared memories are only one part of friendship.
sentences.ja: 質問し、新しい関心を学び、共通の思い出は友情の一部にすぎないと認められます。

sentences.en: A lasting relationship depends less on controlling another person's time than on mutual respect and thoughtful communication.
sentences.ja: 続く関係は相手の時間を支配することより相互尊重と丁寧な意思疎通にかかります。

sentences.en: Distance changes the form of friendship, but it does not have to remove the care that gives the relationship value.
sentences.ja: 距離は友情の形を変えても、関係に価値を与える思いやりを必ず奪うわけではありません。

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Long-distance friendship can continue through respectful communication and realistic expectations.
Moving away always ends a friendship.
Every old friendship should remain unchanged.
questions.explanation_ja: 異なる生活を尊重した関係の継続が主題です。

questions.prompt: What changes after one friend moves away?
options: Both friends attend the same club.

questions.prompt: Why can a delayed reply be misinterpreted?
options: A reader may not know the practical circumstances behind it.
The sender does not care about anyone.
questions.explanation_ja: 相手の事情が見えないためです。

questions.prompt: Why does the moved friend have less free time?
options: More festivals in the old school.
New club activities and a longer journey home.
questions.explanation_ja: 部活動と長い帰宅時間です。

questions.prompt: What do the friends agree not to demand?
options: An immediate response to every message.
questions.explanation_ja: 即時の返信を要求しないことです。

questions.prompt: Why might constant availability harm friendship?
options: It can create pressure rather than support.
Friends cannot talk on the phone.
New schools never provide free time.
questions.explanation_ja: 常に返信する圧力になるためです。
mutualは相互のという意味です。

questions.prompt: What do the friends decide about longer conversations?
options: They must talk for hours every night.
They may arrange them occasionally instead of counting daily messages.
questions.explanation_ja: 時々長い会話を計画します。

questions.prompt: Why doesn't changing interests necessarily end friendship?
options: Friends can learn about each other's new experiences and keep respecting one another.
questions.explanation_ja: 変化を受け止め互いを知り直せるためです。

questions.prompt: What does the final sentence emphasize?
options: Distance may change communication without destroying care or connection.
questions.explanation_ja: 距離と友情の価値を区別する結論です。
